definitions.explanation: Having a poor, worn-out, or neglected appearance that makes something look pathetic or undignified.

examples.japanese: {見窄|みすぼ}らしい{格好|かっこう}をしている。
{長年|ながねん}{手入|てい}れしていないので、{庭|にわ}が{見窄|みすぼ}らしくなった。
examples.english: The garden looks run-down because it hasn't been maintained for years.

examples.japanese: {外見|がいけん}は{見窄|みすぼ}らしいが、{料理|りょうり}は{絶品|ぜっぴん}の{店|みせ}だ。
examples.english: The restaurant looks shabby from the outside, but the food is superb.

notes:
USAGE:
Describes the visual impression of something looking poor, worn, or undignified. Can apply to clothing, buildings, appearance, or possessions. Has a strongly negative connotation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見窄|みすぼ}らしい{格好|かっこう} (shabby outfit)
- {見窄|みすぼ}らしい{身|み}なり (wretched appearance)
- {見窄|みすぼ}らしい{建物|たてもの} (run-down building)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {粗末|そまつ}: crude, poor-quality — focuses on quality rather than appearance
- ボロボロ: tattered, falling apart — more extreme physical deterioration
